title: Minimum Time to Visit a Cell In a Grid
statement:
You get an `m x n` matrix `grid` of non-negative integers. The value `grid[row][col]` is the earliest second at which the cell `(row, col)` may be entered: you may stand on it at time `t` only when `t >= grid[row][col]`.

At second 0 you are on the top-left cell `(0, 0)`. Every second you have to step to one of the up to four cells that share a side with your current cell (up, down, left or right, staying inside the grid); each step lasts exactly one second and standing still is not allowed.

Return the smallest time at which you can be on the bottom-right cell `(m - 1, n - 1)`, or `-1` if that cell can never be reached.
notes:
## Intuition

This is a shortest-path problem where an edge cannot always be used right away. Two facts make it simple:

- If both neighbours of the start need more than 1 second, the first forced step is impossible and the answer is `-1`. Otherwise you can always "wait" by stepping back and forth between two cells, so every cell is eventually reachable.
- Each step changes `row + col` by one, so you are on a cell only at times with the parity of `row + col`. Bouncing costs 2 seconds per round trip, so if a neighbour opens at `open > time + 1`, you arrive at `open` when `open - time` is odd, and at `open + 1` when it is even.

With that arrival rule, Dijkstra on the grid gives the earliest time at each cell. The brute force simulates the set of reachable cells second by second.

## Approach

1. Return `-1` when `grid[0][1] > 1` and `grid[1][0] > 1`.
2. Set `dist[0][0] = 0` and push `[0, 0, 0]` onto a min-heap ordered by time.
3. Pop the earliest `[time, row, col]`; skip it if it is stale, return `time` if it is the bottom-right cell.
4. For each neighbour, compute `wait` (1 when `open - time` is even) and `arrive = max(time + 1, open + wait)`.
5. If `arrive` beats `dist` for that neighbour, store it and push it.

## Example 1, step by step

`grid[0][1] = 1`, so the start is not boxed in. From `(0,0)` at 0 we reach `(0,1)` at 1 and `(1,1)` at 2. From `(1,1)`, `(1,2)` opens at 2 but `2 - 2` is even, so `arrive = max(3, 3) = 3`. From `(1,2)` at 3, `(1,3)` opens at 5: `5 - 3` is even, so `arrive = 6`. From `(1,3)` at 6, `(2,3)` opens at 6: `6 - 6` is even, so `arrive = 7`. That is the smallest popped time for the target, so the answer is `7`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m·n·log(m·n)): each cell is pushed a few times and each heap operation is logarithmic.
- Space: O(m·n) for `dist` and the heap.

## Pitfalls

- Waiting in place is not allowed; only the start check decides whether bouncing is possible at all.
- When `open - time` is even you arrive one second later than `open`, because of parity.
- `(open - time) % 2` can be `-1` or `-0` when `open < time`; `Math.max` with `time + 1` makes those cases harmless.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `dist` | earliest known arrival time for each cell |
| `heap` | min-heap of `[time, row, col]` entries |
| `time`, `row`, `col` | the popped cell and the time you stand on it |
| `open` | the neighbour's opening time from `grid` |
| `wait` | 1 extra second needed to match parity, else 0 |
| `arrive` | when you can stand on the neighbour |

narration.5: dist holds the earliest known arrival time for every cell, starting at infinity.
narration.9: push adds an entry to the min-heap and lifts it while it is earlier than its parent.
narration.19: pop removes the earliest entry and sinks the moved last entry back into place.
narration.38: We stand on the top-left cell at second 0.
narration.40: Dijkstra: keep taking the earliest unsettled arrival until the heap is empty.
narration.41: Take the cell we can reach soonest among those waiting.
narration.42: A later duplicate of an already improved cell is stale, so skip it.
narration.43: The first time the bottom-right cell is popped, its time is the minimum.
narration.47: Ignore neighbours that fall outside the grid.
narration.49: Bouncing back and forth costs 2 seconds, so if open and time have the same parity we need one extra second.
narration.50: Arrive one second from now, or as soon as the neighbour is open with the right parity, whichever is later.
narration.51: Only an earlier arrival than we already know is worth recording.
narration.53: Queue the neighbour with its new arrival time.
narration.57: Unreachable after the start check is impossible, but return -1 for completeness.
